reasoning: The story here is a workflow platform that has quietly become the system of record for how large enterprises get work done. ServiceNow started in IT service management but the durable narrative is that it sits on top of fragmented enterprise processes, IT, HR, customer service, security, and stitches them into a single workflow layer with very high switching costs. Who buys from them? Large organizations with sticky, multi-year, expanding contracts (the net revenue retention story). That installed base, the data exhaust running through it, and 98%-plus renewal economics are the moat. Now to the investor's real question: will AI disrupt this business? My answer is that AI is a two-sided coin and you must let it move the scenarios, not the headline. On the opportunity side, ServiceNow owns the workflow and the proprietary data that AI agents need to act on; Now Assist is a monetization layer that raises price per seat and pulls margin up, and AI agents that automate workflows arguably widen the addressable market rather than shrink it, because the platform becomes the orchestration plane for the agents. On the threat side, the bear case is real: if autonomous AI agents learn to execute work directly and bypass the structured workflow software entirely, and if generative AI commoditizes ITSM the way it has commoditized simpler SaaS, then growth and pricing power both compress. I have not assumed away either outcome; I have priced both. Connecting the story to the numbers. Trailing revenue is about $13.96B growing ~22%. I model base-case growth fading from 18% to 6% over ten years, a bear path from 13% to 4% (AI commoditization bites), and a bull path from 23% to 6% (Now Assist compounds). The critical Damodaran discipline is margins: reported FCF of $4.53B looks like a 32% margin, but stock-based compensation is ~$1.96B, roughly 14% of revenue, and SBC is a real cost to owners. So I charge it. My honest owner-earnings FCFF margin starts near 18.5% and I let it expand to a 27% target in the base case (AI-driven operating leverage), 22% in the bear, 32% in the bull. Risk: cost of equity via CAPM is 4.49% risk-free plus a 0.93 real beta times a 5.5% ERP, about 9.6%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.2%; the firm is ~98% equity-financed, so WACC is ~9.5%. Terminal growth is set at the risk-free rate of 4.49%, never above it. The math says: base case intrinsic value ~$145.49 per share, bear ~$63.15, bull ~$196.57. Probability-weighted at 25/50/25, fair value is ~$137.67 versus a $102.15 price, a margin of safety near 35%. Cross-check: EV/Sales is 7.3x, which for a mid-20s grower with this retention sits inside the high-quality SaaS peer band, not stretched two standard deviations above. The stock just fell from $114 to $102, which widens the discount. Even after charging SBC as the real expense it is, the platform is worth more than the market is paying. Bullish, but sized for the genuine AI tail risk, hence confidence 68 rather than higher.
